predecessors.name: Kingdom of Westphalia
predecessors.text: the principality of Wolfenbüttel, 'from 1807 to 1813 ... held as part of the Kingdom of Westphalia'

successors.name: Weimar Republic
successors.text: the state as it stood in 1870, unchanged to November 1918 (Free State of Brunswick)

ledger.x: 26 October 1813: Duke Frederick William resumes his rule at Brunswick as Westphalia falls.
1814: the German page lists 'around 1814' the duchy's non-contiguous parts, among them the Amt Thedinghausen and the Amt Calvörde.
1815: the restored Wolfenbüttel principality is a sovereign Duchy of Brunswick.

wars.name: War of the Sixth Coalition
wars.outcome: After Prussia 'had ended French domination in the region' the Duke returned to Braunschweig in December 1813 and Brunswick left Westphalia.

wars.name: Austro-Prussian War
wars.outcome: Brunswick joined the Prussian side ('im Deutschen Krieg'), which preserved its formal statehood; the neighbouring Kingdom of Hanover was annexed by Prussia in 1866 while Brunswick 'remained sovereign and independent'.

certainty.note: The restoration 'in the old borders' is described without a boundary; the 1814 outline is Cliopatria's.

A state of the German Confederation with fixed Landesgrenzen and exclaves (Thedinghausen, Calvörde) inside Hanover and Prussia; the pages give no surveyed line, so sharpness rests on the state's recognised status.
